To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PPy nanostructures are efficient photocatalysts for water depolluting.
PPy nanostructures exhibit a high activity for photocatalysis and can be used as photocatalyst for organic pollutant degradations under both UV and Visible light.
PPy nanostructures are very efficient photocatalysts for the degradation of pollutants in water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of nanostructured conjugated polymers (CPNs) and the development of their application in photocatlysis.
the synthesis and characterization of novel nanostructures of PPy and their application as photocatalyst.
the design and synthesis of novel photocatalyst materials for organic pollutant photodegradation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photocatalytic activity is directly correlated to the size and morphology of the PPy nanostructures.
the photocatalytic activity is strongly related to the morphology of the PPy samples, the presence of the soft template and to the irradiation wavelength.
the photocatalytic activity is directly correlated to the nanostructuration and morphology of the PPy nanostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photocatalytic activity for PPy NS c and Ppy NS g is mainly attributed to the nanostructure of these materials and their ability to generate electron hole pairs under light irradiation.
the nanostructured PPy can be used as photocatalyst for degradation of organic pollutants in water.
the nanostructurated conjugated polymers are a very good alternative to the semiconductor-based photocatalysts for the photodegradation of organic pollutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPy nanostructures are efficient photocatalysts and can be used as an alternative to TiO _{2} in photocatalysis.
the photocatalytic properties of CPNs are not only dependent on their chemical structure but also on their nanostructures.
PPy nanostructures are promising candidates for water depolluting.
